resolutions.subject: Delaware compiled pathway 'Discretionary court expungement under 11 Del. C. § 4374'

operativeAuthority.subsection: § 4374 generally (discretionary petition on a manifest-injustice showing, with the Attorney General as opposing party). § 4374(c) is the forum provision and is the discriminator: it compels Family Court filing only where every charge and conviction sought was disposed of in Family Court, leaving the general § 4374 Superior Court route as the one this pathway implements. § 4374(f) and (h) carry the prosecutor-initiated route and are not implemented here.

resolutions.license: Shared operative citation plus forum identity, both re-checkable. (1) The pathway id and label carry the bare citation '11 Del. C. § 4374' with no subsection; exactly one DE registry track carries the same bare citation as its whole authority — de_discretionary_superior_court, authority ['11 Del. C. § 4374, most recently amended at 85 Del. Laws, c. 142, § 10']. (2) Forum: the DE profile fixes this pathway in Superior Court — packetGenerator.filingDestinationRules[0] 'Mandatory is handled by the SBI; discretionary is filed with the Superior Court (Family Court for juvenile)'; packetGenerator.sourceFormStatements[7] 'Expungement Petition packet (Superior ... available at courts.delaware.gov under Superior Court → Expungement)'; sourceSections[13] captions its worked example 'SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF DELAWARE ... PETITION FOR DISCRETIONARY EXPUNGEMENT (11 Del. C. 4374)'. The strings '281', 'Form 281' and 'FORM-281' — the Family Court track's only primary filing — appear nowhere in DE-delaware.json. (3) The prosecutor track is excluded on actor: the pathway makes the Attorney General the objector ('the Attorney General may object within 120 days'), while de_attorney_general_expungement is defined by the prosecutor being the movant and the participant not filing. A generator re-applies this as: bare-section citation match, then forum match against packetGenerator.filingDestinationRules, then movant match.
